tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

## 1. Corpus MM3-H — discipline d'accès
## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.

**Options**

1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.

**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?

**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

---

## 5b. Scénarios d'usage (exigences de validation, pas une description de l'implémentation actuelle de Weld)

| ID | Structure | Séquence | Attendu |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Graphe de scène | Pool de nœuds `{data, parent : handle, child : handle}` sur une allocation ; deux nœuds liés dans les deux sens par handles ; `resolve` `Modify` d'un nœud, écriture de `data`, `unresolve` ; `freeSlot` d'un nœud encore désigné par le handle de l'autre ; `resolve` de ce handle ; `freeSlot` pendant une résolution active | tout `ok` ; `resolve` du handle périmé : `fail` ; `freeSlot` pendant résolution : `reject` |
| W2 | ECS archetype + sparse set | Archetype à deux colonnes (SoA) sur une allocation ; `split` des colonnes ; système A écrit la colonne 1 pendant que le système B lit la colonne 2 ; `resolveMany` `Modify` de trois entités distinctes d'un pool d'entités ; déplacement d'une entité vers un autre archetype (transferts des champs de la ligne) pendant qu'une vue de colonne est active, puis après sa libération | lectures et écritures disjointes `ok` ; `resolveMany` `ok` ; déplacement pendant la vue : `reject` ; après : `ok` |
| W3 | Arène de frame | `alloc`, `newArena`, trois `issue`, trois vues rangées (`store`) dans une structure locale ; `reset` pendant que les vues vivent ; `endUse` de la structure ; `reset` ; réémission | `reset` pendant : `reject` ; après : `ok` ; réémission `ok` |

## 6. Registre des obligations inter-spécifications

| Obligation | Destination |
|---|---|
| `stat` (composante concurrente des obligations opaques) ; transférabilité, partageabilité ; H39, H41 | spec 2 |
| Protection forte des paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; H27b ; H38, H40, H42 ; `defer` | spec 3 |
| `dec` (validité de représentation) ; `SameSizeAlong` ; une référence se range dans un emplacement de type référence ; `kind` comme point d'accroche ; le type d'un pointeur porte la forme d'une région non contiguë (le pointeur n'en désigne que l'adresse la plus basse) | spec 4 |
| `dec` (alignement des accès) ; taille d'un pointeur et encodage `decode` ; largeur des adresses et épuisement de l'espace ; débordement des générations ; placement (`PlacementOK`), jetons (`TokCompat`) | spec 11 |
| Traduction bas niveau de `noalias` | spec 13 |
| Obligation de libération attachée à certains types ; H43 | spécification des ressources |
| `DeclaredDisjoint` (disjonction des feuilles déclarées) ; `FreeCompat` ; représentation des métadonnées d'arène et de pool | bibliothèque |

## 7. Registre de la reconstruction de référence

0. Exécution de MM2-H (17 cas) contre la reconstruction de MM-02 ; MM23-H15 et H16 rejoués après application des décisions 2 et 3 du jalon 2.
1. Écarts du brouillon MM-03 trouvés au jalon 2 (passe 1, (f) 1–6) : utilisabilité des feuilles lues et écrites ; empreintes faites de feuilles ; une racine par `alloc` ; marques de mort transitives ; `RootLive` ; bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.
2. Locaux d'`enterFrame` possédés directement par le cadre (O6, à écrire dans la v0.3).
3. Décisions 1 à 4 du jalon 2 : disjonction déclarée par feuilles ; pointeur d'une région vide ; adresse la plus basse ; feuille de référence de la taille d'un pointeur.
4. Théorèmes à énoncer : induction « toute feuille `Init` atteinte a été déclarée ou écrite » ; correspondance `Step` ↔ `Reachable`.
5. Noms Lean des textes normatifs déplacés en annexe de correspondance.

**Why:** the briefs require French commit messages (one per step), docstrings citing `MM-0x.y` rules, statement changes justified in the report, and say `formal/reports/` is exploration never merged into `main`. Later briefs add "arbitrages" that answer earlier report questions.

**How to apply:** start a new pass from the latest branch tip; run an adversarial review workflow over module and report before delivering; `lake` is not on PATH, call `~/.elan/bin/lake`; keep the Lake library name `Ern`. `formal/Ern/.gitkeep` keeps showing as deleted: restore it with `git checkout`, never commit the deletion. A post-commit hook can make `git commit` exceed 2 minutes: give it a long timeout. The axiom rule ({propext, Quot.sound} only) forbids core lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (`List.getElem?_mapIdx`, `List.eq_nil_iff_forall_not_mem`, `List.nodup_range`, `List.pairwise_lt_range`): sweep `#print axioms` over every theorem and replace them with local lemmas. Mathlib tactics (`set`, `tauto`) are unavailable. Reviews keep catching report errors: quote old forms from the old commit, count declarations with a command, and base an evidence claim only on a check that would fail on the defect. After fixing review findings, run a second targeted review of the fixes: in MM-03 pass 2 a fix over-rejected legitimate programs. Before calling a clause "missing" from an arbitrage, re-read every earlier arbitrage still in force: in pass 3 the clause needed for exitFrame_no_dangling was A4's root-holder rule, which A1 puts in WF3 and pass 2 had left out. `timeout` does not exist on this Mac: run `lake build` directly (about 2.5 min). When an arbitrage enlarges a definition used in hypotheses (pass 4: `Inv3` gained `NoDangling`), theorems whose text is unchanged silently narrow: give them only the conjunct they use. Before retiring a counterexample whose witness breaks a new invariant clause, look for another witness: pass-4 review found one and flagged the weakening as major. Check obligations against the initial state: the base frame of `S3.init` owns no place, so an obligation about it can be vacuous on reached states. A review fix can itself pick a semantic reading (pass 5: the kind conjunct of `IsInternalFor` rejected a `newArena` that D3 leaves undecided): check every fix for verdicts it changes on cases the text is silent on. Module docstrings must cite the report's own numbering, not the review's decision numbers. Arbiter-supplied theorems can be false: check them on small reached states (owned storage, a parameter that is the ancestor of another) before trying a proof. Every factual claim in the report needs a module witness, or reviewers flag it; never say "blocked until X" without checking escape sequences such as ending the owner value. When a precondition gains clauses, lemmas taking it as a hypothesis narrow silently: name the old precondition (pass 7: `EnterPreBase`) and give the lemmas only what they use. A guard on one operation (G2 on `store`) is usually bypassable through another (a helper authority then `release`/`endUse`/`free`/exit): look for such bypasses before claiming a configuration is excluded. A new check on an operation with a defined failure (`issue` → `fail`) must not turn that failure into `reject`. Use one adversarial reviewer per arbitrage lens; each found distinct real issues in pass 7. When a restriction rejects an old counterexample, try to rebuild a witness that satisfies the new clause before restating it as a rejection (pass 8: a same-shape destination restored `transfer_not_inv3_preserving`). Drop hypotheses a proof does not use. When cases disappear because their state is no longer reached, replay their verdicts on a new reachable state and list the drops. Machine-check every changed verdict the report lists, including the old witnesses' rejected steps. Never state "only clause X fails" as `X → Pre` next to `¬ X`: that is vacuous; name the other clauses (pass 8: `TransferPreBase` with an iff) and state them. Run a second targeted check after fixing verification findings: in pass 8 it caught that vacuous form. `omega` proving a conjunction goal pulls `Classical.choice`: split the goal first. `meta` is a keyword in this Lean: never name a hypothesis `meta`. `set` (Mathlib) is unavailable: use `obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x = e := ⟨_, rfl⟩`. `if_pos`/`if_neg`/`ite_cond_eq_true` are deprecated: use `simp only [h, ↓reduceIte]`. When `S3.Usable.mono` is applied with `rfl` for `hP`, give `(s := …) (s' := …)` explicitly or it unifies the wrong way. Simulation theorems: never quantify obligations over all translations (vacuous); put them as per-step premises of the run with parameters fixed once, and give a concrete multi-step run as witness. A universal encoding obligation (`∀ addr, decode (enc addr) = addr`) is unsatisfiable by a finite computable decode: state it per value. `lake env lean` uses the last built olean: rebuild the module before a scratch file uses new declarations. Never use an unquoted heredoc for Lean or docstrings: backticks run as shell commands; use `<<'EOF'` and pass paths by environment variable. `example`s escape a `collectAxioms` sweep: rename them to theorems in a scratch copy to check their axioms. `awk length` counts bytes, not characters: count line length in Python. Each check round finds errors in the previous round's wording: when a sentence is fixed in a docstring, grep the report for the same claim; quote arbitrages exactly (L2 said "hypothèse des énoncés", not "hors langage"); classify every item a deliverable asks to classify instead of moving it aside; a summary must not present a hypothesis restated in a conclusion as a result. Count theorem constants with internal ones (`isInternal`) and say which count you give. A callee cannot move a value out of a parameter's footprint (`ActiveDerivedOutside` counts the parameter itself): build values to transfer as callee locals. Authority ids shift with every alloc/issue/split: check them with `#eval` of `prun` prefixes before writing a case. A literal invariant from the material can fail under the full kernel extension: keep the literal statement with counterexamples and prove the parts that hold, under their own names.

# Jalon 3 log (ub-mode)

1. Created branch formal/validation_0.1 from formal/refinement_0.1 (brief: new draft branch).
2. Read MM-03.3 v0.3 révisée in full, the jalon-3 material v2, and the kernel API of MM03.lean
   (derive, split, release, transfer, store, enter/exit, endUse, free, alloc, arenas, Reachable)
   to build the pool on kernel operations only.
3. Design of HandlePool: pool entries outside S3 (kernel unchanged); slots = children of the
   storage (kids), first free slot for allocSlot; resolve = derive companion (whole storage) +
   derive entry; resolveMany = derive companion + split; unresolve = releases; freeSlot = endUse;
   right check = companion's DerivePre (so H31a rejects whatever the handles). Extension PReach =
   all kernel steps + pool ops, so pool ops are kernel step chains (PReach -> Reachable).
4. Finding while designing: PoolInv clauses 2-3 are not preserved when the program can use the
   companion (kernel derive from it onto a free entry) or through exitFrame re-anchoring.
5. Step 1 done (6d79960): HandlePool with PReach, invariants (PoolWF, NoStale, CompExcl,
   EntriesDisjoint), named theorems, literal PoolInv with three counterexamples, runner prun with
   soundness (lets decide build reached states fast). Axioms clean on 734 constants.
6. Step 2 done: MM3-H in Ern/MM03/Horrors.lean, 54 cases + J expansion, every state reached by
   prun from S3.init. Findings: H16 not expressible (callee cannot move out of a parameter:
   ActiveDerivedOutside); H07 rebuilt on a callee local; W2 column authority blocks the move; W3
   literal reading gives reject after endUse of the structure (blocks held by locals); H51 view
   makes v unwritable and un-endable until frame exit; H01 reborrow variant accepted.
7. Step 3 done: MM23-H in Ern/MM23/Horrors.lean; executable SimRun runner (srun) with soundness;
   layout computed from the final places so no per-case tables; 7 runs cover all encoded cases;
   H15/H16 known gaps measured (address 0 / head +8).
8. Step 4 done: LockOptions. Both options: no false rejection on the must-accept list. Option 2
   prevents H50 only (local); option 3 prevents H49 (closing store), H50, H51 (cycle root-of-storage
   / view) and is not local. Inline runs of MM03/Horrors named for reuse.
9. Report drafted (French), then four read-only adversarial reviewers, one per lens (pool
   exclusivity/fidelity, MM3-H twins, NoLock measure, MM23-H). No blocking finding; no bypass of
   pool_resolve_modify_exclusive. Accepted findings: freeSlot unusable on derived internal or
   writeShared right (spec defect, witnesses + (g)); pools/arenas sharing internal (witnesses);
   "périmé" two readings; allocSlot content Init; H51/H07 docstrings; W3 variant kept views; H17
   minimal twin; H01 reborrow and W2 stated per reading; opt3_not_local witness was on a state the
   kernel already rejects (replaced); cost reading (operation vs function) reported; MM23 H04/H06
   statements strengthened, step_ok_of for per-step ok, H02 persistence, H07 fail under KNS.
   Fix commit 6cb3f1b (modules + report). H09 step_ok_of hit a heartbeat timeout until the contract
   was passed explicitly (unification of inferred K unfolded the run).
10. Second targeted check launched as a workflow (ultracode): 4 checkers + one refuter per finding.

theorem H01_reborrow : PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] [.enter [] S2, .derive 0 0 .modify,
    .derive 1 1 .observe, .enter [1, 2] []]) :=
  run_reach (by decide) (by decide)

/-- H02, frame 1 with the structure of H01 and an `Observe` authority 1 on the whole. -/
def h02 : PS := run K0 [] [.enter [] S2, .derive 0 0 .observe]

/-- **H02** (A; I1, effective mode; N3). `Observe` on the whole, then `Modify` on a part: rejected,
the effective mode of the root on the part being `Observe` (MM-03.3.5). Expected: reject; obtained:
reject. Twin without the observation: accepted. -/
theorem H02 : PReach K0 [] h02 ∧ DeriveStep 0 1 .modify h02.s .reject ∧
    DeriveStep 0 1 .modify h01t.s (.ok (deriveEff h01t.s 0 1 .modify)) :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- H03: frame 1, structure X (0) with the parts `p` (1) and 2, leaf Y (3); the frame derives 2,
`Modify` on `p`, and stores it into Y. -/
def h03o : List Op := [.enter [] (S2 ++ [lf]), .derive 0 1 .modify, .store 2 3]
def h03 : PS := run K0 [] h03o
def h03t : PS := run K0 [] [.enter [] (S2 ++ [lf])]

/-- **H03** (A; I1, F4; N3). The value of Y holds a `Modify` derived on the part `p` of X; a write
of `p` through the root of X is rejected (no effective mode, MM-03.3.5; O10). Expected: reject;
obtained: reject. Twin without the stored authority: accepted. The `store` is not what makes the
write fail: after the `derive` alone, the write is already rejected (I1, effective mode), so the case
does not exercise F4 itself. -/
theorem H03 : PReach K0 [] h03 ∧ Write3Step 0 [1] h03.s .reject ∧
    Write3Step 0 [1] h03t.s (.ok (write3Eff h03t.s [1])) :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide)⟩

without the transfer of the part: the access dies with the container, and `A` is released. -/
theorem H10 : PReach K0 [] h10 ∧ ReleaseStep 3 h10.s .reject ∧
    PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (h10p ++ [.endUse 1, .release 3])) :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), .reject (by decide), run_reach (by decide) (by decide)⟩

/-- H11: frame 1, arena value 0, allocator 1, values `v1` (2) and `v2` (3); storage 4 with the
leaves 5 and 6, owned by 0, `internal` 4; blocks 5 on `[5]` to `v1` and 6 on `[6]` to `v2`; `v1`
is transferred into the leaf 6 of the block of `v2`. -/
def h11p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)], .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4,
  .issue 0 0 [5] 2, .issue 0 0 [6] 3, .transfer 2 6]
def h11 : PS := run K0 [] h11p

/-- **H11** (B; usage, A10; Lib). An arena buffer stored into another block of the same arena: the
`transfer` is accepted, `reset` is rejected while a block lives. Expected: `transfer` `ok`, `reset`
reject; obtained: the same. Twin: after the end of both blocks (`endUse` of `v2`, then of the leaf
6), `reset` is accepted. -/
theorem H11 : PReach K0 [] h11 ∧ ResetAtStep K0 0 0 h11.s .reject ∧
    PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] (h11p ++ [.endUse 3, .endUse 6, .reset 0 0])) :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), .reject (by decide), run_reach (by decide) (by decide)⟩

Twin without the access: accepted. -/
theorem H15 : PReach KF2 [] h15 ∧ FreeStep KF2 2 7 h15.s .reject ∧
    PReach KF2 [] (run KF2 [] (h14p ++ [.alloc 0 2 [lf], .free 2 7])) :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), .reject (by decide), run_reach (by decide) (by decide)⟩

/-- Contracts with the place 3 deallocable by the authority 7. -/
abbrev KF3 : K := KT [] [] [] [3] [(3, 7)]

/-- H16: frame 1, allocator 0, `x` (1) written, result `R` (2); storage 3 owned by `x`, written; the
caller derives 4, `Modify` on `x`, and 5, `Modify` on `R`, and calls frame 2, with the local 4. -/
def h16p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .alloc 0 1 [lf],
  .write 3 [3], .derive 1 1 .modify, .derive 2 2 .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf]]
def h16a : PS := run KF3 [] h16p
/-- H16 as it can run: the callee frees the storage through its parameter on `x`, then returns. -/
def h16 : PS := run KF3 [] (h16p ++ [.free 3 7, .exit])
/-- Twin of H16: the callee returns without freeing. -/
def h16t : PS := run KF3 [] (h16p ++ [.exit])

/-- **H16** (C; A5, A6; N3). The callee receives by transfer a value owning a storage, frees it,
returns the value; the caller reads that storage. Expected: `ok`, then reject. Obtained (report,
(b)): the reception is rejected, a parameter being an active derived authority on the source held
outside it (O4.4, `ActiveDerivedOutside`), so the callee cannot take a value of the caller. With
the free made through the parameter on `x`, the callee's steps are `ok` and the caller's read of the
storage is rejected for every authority. Twin without the `free`: the read is accepted. -/
theorem H16 : PReach KF3 [] h16a ∧ TransferStep KF3 1 4 h16a.s .reject ∧
aggregate: the written field is transferred. Expected: `ok`; obtained: `ok`. -/
theorem H47 : PReach K0 [] (run K0 [] h47o) :=
  run_reach (by decide) (by decide)

/-! ## I. Progress (`NoLock`, material §5) -/

/-- Pass-7 arena `fa`: frame 1, arena value 0, allocator 1, values 2 and 3; storage 4 with the nodes
5 and 6; blocks 5 on `[5]` to 2 and 6 on `[6]` to 3. -/
def fao : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 1 0 [lf, (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)], .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4,
  .issue 0 0 [5] 2, .issue 0 0 [6] 3]
/-- H48: 7, `Modify` on B from its block, stored into A; 8, `Modify` on A from its block. -/
def h48o : List Op := fao ++ [.derive 6 6 .modify, .store 7 5, .derive 5 5 .modify]
def h48 : PS := run K0 [] h48o
def h48t : PS := run K0 [] (fao ++ [.derive 6 6 .modify, .derive 5 5 .modify])

/-- **H48** (I; G2; N3; covered pass 7, `progress_cycle_whole_nodes`). A cycle of two authorities on
whole nodes by direct `store`: the closing `store` is rejected by its arrival clause. Expected:
reject; obtained: reject. Twin without the first `store`: accepted. -/
theorem H48 : PReach K0 [] h48 ∧ StoreStep 8 6 h48.s .reject ∧ PReach K0 [] h48t ∧
    StoreStep 8 6 h48t.s (.ok (storeEff h48t.s 8 6)) :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), .reject (by decide), run_reach (by decide) (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- H49: the cycle of H48 closed with the helper 9, then released (pass-7 `f7a_cycle_by_release`). -/
def h49o : List Op := h48o ++ [.derive 7 6 .modify, .store 8 6, .release 9]
def h49 : PS := run K0 [] h49o

/-- **H49** (I; §5; N3; covered pass 7). The same cycle, closed through a helper authority then its
`release`: accepted; the authorities 7 and 8 are then exercisable at no mode and `reset` is
rejected. Expected: to arbitrate (§5); obtained: `ok`, with a residual blocking. -/
theorem H49 : PReach K0 [] h49 ∧ ¬ h49.s.ExercisableAt 7 .observe ∧
    ¬ h49.s.ExercisableAt 8 .observe ∧ ResetAtStep K0 0 0 h49.s .reject :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide, .reject (by decide)⟩

/-- H50, `transfer`: frame 1, structure 0 with the field 1, structure 2 with the field 3; 2,
`Modify` on 3, stored into 1; 0 transferred into 2 (pass-7 `held_unexercisable_by_transfer`). -/
def h50ao : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, (some 0, none, 0), lf, (some 2, none, 0)],
  .derive 1 3 .modify, .store 2 1, .transfer 0 2]
def h50a : PS := run K0 [] h50ao
/-- H50, `issue`: the block on the node 5 issued to the node 5 itself (pass-7
`held_unexercisable_by_issue`). -/
def h50bo : List Op := fao.take 5 ++ [.issue 0 0 [5] 5]
def h50b : PS := run K0 [] h50bo

/-- **H50** (I; §5; N3, Lib; covered pass 7). An authority transferred or issued into the place it
covers: accepted, and then exercisable at no mode. Expected: to arbitrate (§5); obtained: `ok`,
with a residual blocking. -/
theorem H50 : PReach K0 [] h50a ∧ ¬ h50a.s.ExercisableAt 2 .observe ∧
    PReach K0 [] h50b ∧ ¬ h50b.s.ExercisableAt 5 .observe :=
  ⟨run_reach (by decide) (by decide), by decide, run_reach (by decide) (by decide), by decide⟩

/-- H51: frame 1, allocator 0, `v` (1) written; storage 2 with the element 3, owned by `v`, of root 2
held by `v`; the helper 3, `Modify` on the storage; 4, `Observe` on `v`, stored into the element 3;
the helper released. -/
def h51o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, (some 2, none, 0)], .derive 2 2 .modify, .derive 1 1 .observe, .store 4 3,
  .release 3]
def h51 : PS := run K0 [] h51o
/-- H51 without the helper: 3, `Observe` on `v`. -/
def h51n : PS := run K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, (some 2, none, 0)], .derive 1 1 .observe]

/-- **H51** (I; §5; N3). An element of a storage owned by `v` holds a view on `v`. The direct `store`
is rejected: the view already takes away the frame's `Modify` on `v`, hence on the storage `v` owns
(`HasRight` before the step, B2), and the arrival clause of G2 fails too; with a helper on the
storage, then its `release`, the configuration is reached. Then `v` can be neither written, ended by `endUse`, nor relieved of the view (`release`
rejected), while the view stays exercisable at `Observe`; the exit of the frame releases it.
Expected: to arbitrate (§5); obtained: `ok`, with a residual blocking until the exit. -/
theorem H51 : PReach K0 [] h51n ∧ StoreStep 3 3 h51n.s .reject ∧ PReach K0 [] h51 ∧
    Write3Step 1 [1] h51.s .reject ∧ ReleaseStep 4 h51.s .reject ∧ EndUseStep K0 1 h51.s .reject ∧
/-- W2: frame 1, allocator 0, owners 1 and 2 of two archetypes, entity pool value 3, handle leaves
4, 5, 6. Archetype 7 (columns 8 with 9, 10 and 11 with 12, 13) owned by 1; archetype 14 (columns
15 with 16, 17 and 18 with 19, 20) owned by 2; entity storage 21 (entries 22, 23, 24) owned by 3,
pool on it. `split` of the archetype into the columns (10 and 11), the second written, a read view
12 on it; system A writes the first column while system B reads through the view; `resolveMany
Modify` of three distinct entities. -/
def w2o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1],
  .write 2 [2], .write 3 [3],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, (some 7, none, 0), (some 8, none, 0), (some 8, none, 0), (some 7, none, 0),
    (some 11, none, 0), (some 11, none, 0)],
  .alloc 0 2 [lf, (some 14, none, 0), (some 15, none, 0), (some 15, none, 0), (some 14, none, 0),
    (some 18, none, 0), (some 18, none, 0)],
  .alloc 0 3 [lf, (some 21, none, 0), (some 21, none, 0), (some 21, none, 0)], .newPool 21 9,
  .allocSlot 0 0 4, .allocSlot 0 0 5, .allocSlot 0 0 6,
  .split 7 [[9, 10], [12, 13]], .write 11 [12, 13], .derive 11 11 .observe,
  .write 10 [9, 10], .read 12 [12, 13], .resolveMany 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 1, 0⟩, ⟨0, 2, 0⟩] .modify]
def w2 : PS := run K0 [] w2o
def w2a : PS := run K0 [] (w2o ++ [.release 12])

/-- **W2** (§5b, ECS archetype and sparse set; Lib). Expected: disjoint reads and writes `ok`;
`resolveMany` `ok`; the move of a field of the row while the column view is active: reject; after
its release: `ok`. Obtained: disjoint accesses, `resolveMany` and the rejection during the view as
expected. After the release: if "the view of the column" is the read view 12, the move is still
rejected, by the column authority 11 given by `split` (O4.4; report, (b)); if it is the column
authority itself, the move is accepted after its release (and that of the first column authority,
which covers the other field of the row). -/
theorem W2 : PReach K0 [] w2 ∧ TransferStep K0 12 19 w2.s .reject ∧ PReach K0 [] w2a ∧

## Git
Nouvelle branche brouillon `formal/validation_0.1`, créée depuis `formal/refinement_0.1`. Pas de merge, pas de PR. Tout sous `formal/`. `Ern/MM02.lean`, `Ern/MM03.lean` et `Ern/MM23.lean` inchangés. Documents joints, non copiés : `ERN_MM02_v04.md`, MM-03.3 v0.3 révisée, `ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md` (version 2). Le matériel du jalon 3 fait foi pour les cas, le contrat du pool et le cadrage de `NoLock` ; ses règles du §0 s'appliquent toutes.

Code, docstrings, commentaires, messages de commit en anglais. Rapport en français.

1. **`HandlePool`** (§4 du matériel) : état de l'entrée de pool, identité fraîche, opérations `newPool`, `allocSlot`, `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `unresolve`, `freeSlot`, construites sur les opérations du noyau (`derive`, `split`, `release`, `endUse`) sans les modifier ; `PoolInv` ; extension de `Reachable` définie dans le module ; les théorèmes attendus du §4. `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` est énoncé sur tout état atteint, quelle que soit la séquence de `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `release`, `store`, `transfer` et `unresolve`.
2. **MM3-H** : toutes les lignes des sections A à I, plus W1–W3 (§5b), dans `Ern/MM03/Horrors.lean`. Chaque cas : état atteint depuis l'état initial, verdict attendu selon sa source, jumeau positif pour chaque rejet, classe. Les cas déjà couverts sont rejoués depuis l'état initial en réutilisant les témoins existants quand c'est possible. La section J n'est pas encodée ; confirmer qu'aucun de ses cas n'est exprimable dans le noyau, ou signaler celui qui l'est.
3. **MM23-H** : chaque cas comme exécution traduite par `simulation`, dans `Ern/MM23/Horrors.lean`. H15 et H16 : encodés avec le verdict obtenu et marqués « écart connu » (règle 8 du §0). H14 et H17 : non encodés, classés.

/-- Option 2 on `issue` of `region` to `dst` (material §5): the block, the new authority, is not
self-locked in the arrival state. -/
def Opt2Issue (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  ¬ SelfLock (issueEff s ar region dst).1 s.A.length

instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (Opt2Issue s ar region dst) := by
  unfold Opt2Issue; infer_instance

/-! ## Option 3: `NoLock` -/

/-- "`b` bloque `a`" (material §5, option 3): `b ≠ a`, both active, and the footprint of `b` contains
a leaf of the holder of `a`. -/
def Blocks (s : S3) (b a : Nat) : Prop :=
  b ≠ a ∧ s.Active b ∧ s.Active a ∧
    OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun y => ∃ l ∈ s.afp b, l ∈ holderLeaves s y.holder) False

instance (s : S3) (b a : Nat) : Decidable (Blocks s b a) := by unfold Blocks; infer_instance

/-- The authorities blocked by one of `xs`. -/
def blockedBy (s : S3) (xs : List Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range s.A.length).filter fun a => decide (∃ b ∈ xs, Blocks s b a)

/-- The authorities reached from `xs` by at most `n` steps of `Blocks`, `xs` included. -/
def blockReach (s : S3) : Nat → List Nat → List Nat
  | 0, xs => xs
  | n + 1, xs => blockReach s n (xs ++ blockedBy s xs)

/-- Acyclicity of `Blocks` (material §5, option 3): no authority is reached from itself by one or
more steps. Every step leads to an authority of `A`, so a cycle has at most `A.length` steps and the
search with that bound is complete (report, (f)). -/
  | _ => false

/-- The decisions of the option `D` on the checked steps of a run of `K0` from `ps`, each on the
state where the step runs, in order, as long as the steps are `ok` in the kernel. -/
def decisions (D : PS → Op → Bool) (ps : PS) : List Op → List Bool
  | [] => []
  | o :: os =>
    match pexec K0 ps o with
    | some ps' => (if checked o then [D ps o] else []) ++ decisions D ps' os
    | none => []

/-- The run from `S3.init []` of a case. -/
def dec2 (os : List Op) : List Bool := decisions opt2 (PS.init []) os
def dec3 (os : List Op) : List Bool := decisions opt3 (PS.init []) os

/-! ## Cases that must be accepted (material §5) -/

/-- The runs of the cases that must be accepted, with their names: each is a run of
`Ern.MM03.Horrors` reached under `K0`, except H21's arena which is not on the list. -/
def mustAccept : List (String × List Op) :=
  [("H11", h11p ++ [.endUse 3, .endUse 6, .reset 0 0]),
   ("H19", h19p ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0 0]),
   ("H29b", h29bo), ("H35", h35o), ("H36", h36o), ("H37", h37o), ("H44", h44o),
   ("H45", h45o), ("H46", h46o), ("H47", h47o), ("W1", w1o),
   ("W2", w2o ++ [.release 12, .release 11, .release 10, .transfer 9 16, .transfer 12 19]),
   ("W3", w3o ++ [.endUse 5, .endUse 2, .endUse 3, .endUse 4, .reset 0 0, .issue 0 0 [10] 2]),
   ("W3v", w3vo ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0 0, .issue 0 0 [10] 3])]

/-- Every run of the list is `ok` in the kernel at each step, so the decisions cover all its
checked steps. -/
theorem mustAccept_runs : mustAccept.all (fun c => (prun K0 (PS.init []) c.2).isSome) = true := by
  decide

/-- The decisions of option 2 on the checked steps of each case. -/
theorem opt2_decisions : mustAccept.map (fun c => (c.1, dec2 c.2)) =
    [("H11", [true, true, true]), ("H19", [true]), ("H29b", [true]), ("H35", []),
     ("H36", []), ("H37", [true]), ("H44", [true]), ("H45", [true, true, true, true]),
     ("H46", [true]), ("H47", [true]), ("W1", []), ("W2", [true, true]),
     ("W3", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true]), ("W3v", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true])] := by
  decide

/-- The decisions of option 3 on the checked steps of each case. -/
theorem opt3_decisions : mustAccept.map (fun c => (c.1, dec3 c.2)) =
    [("H11", [true, true, true]), ("H19", [true]), ("H29b", [true]), ("H35", []),

     ("W3", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true]), ("W3v", [true, true, true, true, true, true, true])] := by
  decide

/-- No false rejection (material §5, criterion): neither option rejects a checked step of a case that
must be accepted. -/
